newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil declines comment on Feb trade gap report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil declines comment on Feb trade gap report.

text.p: Brazil's Ministry of Industry and Commerce Tuesday declined to comment on a report the trade gap in February had hit $1.2 billion by mid-month and insisted soft second week exports would pick up.

A ministry spokeswoman, quoting foreign trade secretary Mauricio Cortes, said players should regard Brazil's first quarter trade balance as more relevant than monthly results because of problems with the Siscomex import registration system.
"He (Cortes) refused to comment on the report," the spokeswoman said. "He said the trade balance would become clearer after March."
Globo newspaper reported Tuesday that Brazil had posted a trade gap of $1.2 billion up to February 16 because fuel imports by state oil firm Petrobras were only now being registered.
Without the Petrobras imports, the deficit would stand at $700 million so far.
The Ministry of Industry and Commerce earlier revealed soft second week exports in February of just $418 million, with average daily exports at just $139.3 million.
In the first week of the month, exports were unexpectedly strong at $912 million or $182.4 million a day.
"Cortes said the decrease in exports in the second week was normal at Carnival and that importers had anticipated some Carnival purchases in the first week," the spokeswoman said.
She added Cortes expected exports to pick up in the latter half of the month and reach the levels of the first week.
Brazil posted a $413 million trade gap in January with exports of $3.685 billion, averaging $167.5 million a day.
In 1996, the country saw a record trade deficit of $5.54 billion, expected to widen further this year to at least $8.0 billion.
